target_customer: Automotive aftermarket brands, wholesalers and resellers in Latin America that sell parts on marketplaces such as Mercado Libre, Amazon and Shopee
problem: Brands with thousands of parts struggle to keep catalogs, prices and inventory current across marketplaces, which provide no tools for brands and resellers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for cataloging and marketplace automation, plus a B2B portal that Bloomberg Linea says is about 20 percent of revenue
product_category: Automotive parts catalog and marketplace integration software

founders.name: Gaston Zelerteins
prior_employers: Perception Group (co-founded 2005, Microsoft Gold Partner software house)
founders.background_notes: Source is the YC company page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Javier Neumann
prior_employers: Microsoft (led Dynamics division for Latin America)
education: Electronic engineer with honors, University of Buenos Aires
founders.background_notes: Source is the YC company page.

founders.name: Jonathan Saiegh
founders.background_notes: YC page lists 20+ years in software and e-commerce. Bloomberg Linea says Zelerteins and Saiegh ran a cloud software house together before Alephee.

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalizing and compatibility matching of very large parts catalogs and keeping listings synced via marketplace APIs is laborious but standard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Bloomberg Linea says the catalog work is the main barrier to entry; a catalog of 3M items and Mercado Libre certification help, but the company depends on marketplace APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mercado Libre was the initial investor and partner rather than a copier. It was the only integrated marketplace until 2024 when Shopee was added.

market_need_then: Bloomberg Linea says the company began when Mercado Livre contacted the founders for help building its auto parts category, which indicates a marketplace side need for structured parts catalogs. The company later claims customers selling over 4M USD per month.

branding.domain_note: Uses alephee.com; the YC directory also lists a separate entry named Aleph Solutions.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline e-commerce evolution; B2B corporate tone

rebrands.why: not stated in the sources read; the YC listing and Bloomberg Linea use both names

branding.community_and_virality: Content blog Afterdrive and strategic partner logos (Mercado Livre, Amazon, Shopee); no consumer community

brand_strength.rationale: Business brand with trade content marketing, but a name shared with other Aleph companies and spelled variably.

outcome_analysis: Alephee grew from a Mercado Livre request into a platform used by about 300 brands across eight countries, with Brazil giving 60 percent of revenue, per Bloomberg Linea and the company site. It raised roughly 5M USD since founding and was preparing a 10M to 15M USD round. Experienced software founders and the Mercado Libre relationship helped, while dependence on one marketplace until 2024 is a risk.
notes: Bloomberg Linea (a single outlet) says about 5M USD raised since founding and names the investors above but no round amount or date; I record a 2021 round with null amount because investors are tied to the 2021 YC period only loosely. Aggregators conflict: Seedtable 1.8M USD seed 2021-09, CB Insights 1.83M total, Yespress about 125K USD from YC plus 572K USD from Mercado Libre, Getlatka says bootstrapped. Bloomberg Linea mentions a planned 10M to 15M USD round with no date. The 25M USD Mercado Libre investment in Aleph reported by Forbes Argentina is a different company (Aleph Group, advertising) and is excluded. No dated competitor source found; the company site and Bloomberg Linea name none. Outcome search found no layoffs, sale or shutdown.
